findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider (or explicitly rule out, with rationale) passing Atlassian's `reconcileIssues` parameter on the `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` search the probe already issues, since it is the documented deterministic read-after-write remedy for the named index-lag root cause and may be more robust than a blind exponential-backoff poll.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:260,299,388,471: the codebase already POSTs to '/rest/api/3/search/jql' via `_direct_rest_post_json`
access_check.py:172-188: STEP_JQL_SEARCH polls `client.search_issues(jql)` with a retry loop
The named root cause is Cloud's eventually-consistent Lucene index; `reconcileIssues` on the enhanced JQL endpoint is Atlassian's documented remedy for exactly read-after-write on that endpoint
findings.finding: The JQL-visibility hardening is a blind poll-and-hope backoff, but the probe's search rides `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql`, which the codebase already uses and which supports Atlassian's `reconcileIssues` read-after-write consistency parameter — a structurally-different remedy (force the just-written issueId into the result) the plan does not weigh.
findings.location: Scope item 1 — 'replace the fixed 6x5s loop with an env-tunable EXPONENTIAL-BACKOFF budget'
scenarios: A run where the write lands but the index lags past even the 195s budget: backoff still times out and reports PROBE_FAIL, whereas `reconcileIssues=[issueId]` would surface the issue deterministically

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate Atlassian's documented read-after-write remedy — the `reconcileIssues` parameter on POST /rest/api/3/search/jql (which the codebase already calls in acli_graph.py) — for the probe's STEP_JQL_SEARCH, and record in the plan either why it is used instead of / alongside the backoff budget, or why the blind-wait backoff is preferred despite the first-party mechanism.
evidence: Plan states the root cause as: 'Jira Cloud's Lucene index is eventually consistent and the probe's wait is a FIXED JQL_RETRY_COUNT=6 x JQL_RETRY_SLEEP=5s (no backoff) — shorter than observed Cloud index lag.'

Atlassian developer docs 'Search and Reconcile' (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/search-and-reconcile/): 'after a write operation is performed, subsequent search operations using the API without the reconcileIssues parameter may return stale or outdated data ... for some time' — i.e. a documented deterministic remedy for this exact staleness.

Corroborated independently: NodePit, docs.rs jira_cloud_v3_async, Appfire Power Scripts release notes (reconcileIssues 'accepts up to a maximum of 50 issue IDs and ensures these specific issues display their latest updates'), and the Adaptavist deprecation notes.

The codebase already reaches the enhanced endpoint that accepts this parameter: acli_graph.py issues `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` directly (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map). The probe's own path (acli.py search_issues, lines 445-500) shells out to `jira workitem search` and passes no reconcile parameter — so the mechanism is reachable but unused for the probe.
The plan text nowhere mentions, evaluates, or dismisses reconcileIssues; it commits to a blind-wait budget of up to 195s per probe as the sole remedy.
findings.finding: Scope item 1 chooses a blind exponential-backoff wait (up to 195s) as the entire remedy for Jira Cloud search-index lag without considering Atlassian's documented first-party read-after-write remedy: the `reconcileIssues` parameter on the enhanced POST /rest/api/3/search/jql endpoint, which the codebase already uses elsewhere (acli_graph.py).
findings.location: Scope of this leaf, item 1 ('Harden the search-index-visibility wait'); Acceptance criteria line 1; access_check.py STEP_JQL_SEARCH loop (lines 172-188)
scenarios: A probe run where Cloud index lag exceeds the 195s budget still times out on a false-negative STEP_JQL_SEARCH, exactly the flake the leaf sets out to eliminate — whereas reconcileIssues scoped to the just-created issue id would return the write deterministically without polling.
A future reviewer or maintainer asks why the leaf added a 195s blind wait when the platform offers a bounded read-after-write guarantee, and finds no recorded rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'prior art' note to scope item 1 that (a) names reconcileIssues on the enhanced /search/jql endpoint as the vendor's read-after-write mechanism, (b) states whether the probe's search will pass the newly-created issue id via that parameter (deterministic) or retain blind backoff, and (c) if backoff is kept, justifies it (e.g. the probe searches by label, not id, so reconcileIssues' id-scoped guarantee doesn't cover the label-visibility case) — so the design choice is grounded rather than defaulted.
